title: Equivalent images of two strong cofinal colimit-preserving functors
statement:
Use the universes, infinite regular cardinals, small simplicial sets and filtered quasicategories of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and coherent functors, cocones, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a diagram $p:K\to\mathcal D$, the coherent cocone quasicategory $\mathcal D_{p/}$ has objects $(d,\alpha:p\to\Delta_K d)$, morphisms given by arrows between the vertices and coherent commuting triangles, and all higher compatibilities; $\Delta_K d$ is the constant diagram. For a functor $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$ between filtered quasicategories, weakly cofinal means that each $e\in\mathcal E$ admits an arrow $e\to f(d)$ for some $d\in\mathcal D$. For an infinite regular $\kappa$, $f$ is $\kappa$-cofinal if, for each $\kappa$-small weakly contractible simplicial set $L$ and diagram $r:L\to\mathcal D$, the functor $\mathcal D_{r/}\to\mathcal E_{fr/}$ is weakly cofinal. Weakly contractible means that inverting all arrows gives a contractible space. 

Let $\kappa<\tau$ be infinite regular cardinals and $\mathcal X\xrightarrow{f}\mathcal Y\xleftarrow{g}\mathcal Z$ coherent functors. Suppose all three quasicategories are $\kappa$-filtered and admit colimits of every $\tau$-small $\kappa$-filtered diagram. Suppose $f,g$ preserve those colimits and are $\kappa$-cofinal. Then there exist $x\in\mathcal X$, $z\in\mathcal Z$ and an equivalence $f(x)\simeq g(z)$ in $\mathcal Y$.

source.place: HTT (April 9, 2017), Lemma 5.4.6.3; the alternating transfinite-chain common-image lemma. No matching Stacks tag.

proof.text: For a small diagram $a:K\to\mathcal E$, use the sharp join slice $J_a$ and coherent cocone category $P_a$ of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison]. Its comparison $c:J_a\to P_a$ is an equivalence over $\mathcal E$, and an equivalence on each strict apex fiber. Given a coherent cocone with apex $T$, essential surjectivity in that fiber supplies a sharp cocone $A:K\star\Delta^0\to\mathcal E$ with exactly boundary $a$ and apex $T$, and an equivalence from $c(A)$ to the given cocone within that fiber. Thus we can sharpen the cocones supplied by filteredness and cofinality while retaining their diagrams and vertices. A functor carries the inverse edges and their triangle witnesses to inverse edges and triangle witnesses, so carries this equivalence to an equivalence of image cocones.

source.place: Agent application of the existing join-slice/cocone comparison, HTT Proposition 4.2.1.5 and Corollary 4.2.1.7, to the fixed-end coherence in Lemma 5.4.6.3; archive WANTED.

proof.text: Fix two sharp cocones $A,B$ on the same diagram $a:K\to\mathcal E$, and suppose there is a coherent cocone morphism $c(A)\to c(B)$. The equivalence $c:J_a\to P_a$ of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison] induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{J_a}(A,B)\to\operatorname{Map}_{P_a}(c(A),c(B))$ by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The target has a vertex, so surjectivity on components makes the source nonempty. A vertex of this right-pinched mapping space is an edge $A\to B$; by the stated definition of $J_a$, it is a map $K\star\Delta^1\to\mathcal E$ whose two end cones are exactly $A,B$. After step 1, compose the cocone morphism supplied by cofinality with the chosen cocone equivalences and their inverses, using inner-horn composition. The resulting sharp morphism therefore retains both prescribed end cones, including every simplex. No equality with the original coherent morphism is needed.

proof.text: Regard the cardinal $\kappa$ as its initial ordinal. Write each ordinal $\alpha<\kappa$ uniquely as $\lambda+n$, where $n<\omega$ and $\lambda=0$ or a limit ordinal. Let $E$ consist of those with $n$ even and $O$ those with $n$ odd. Both subsets are unbounded in $\kappa$: from any ordinal, at most two successors reach either parity and still lie below the infinite initial ordinal $\kappa$. The nerves $N(E),N(O),N(\kappa)$ are $\kappa$-filtered by [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]: the vertices of a $\kappa$-small diagram have a bound below $\kappa$, by regularity, and an element of the chosen parity beyond this bound gives the order cocone. Their sets of nondegenerate simplices have cardinality $\kappa$, so they are $\tau$-small. For each $\alpha<\kappa$, the nerve of any subset of $\alpha$ is $\kappa$-small: for $\kappa=\omega$ this is a finite poset; for uncountable $\kappa$ the union of its finite increasing chains has cardinality at most $\max(\aleph_0,|\alpha|)<\kappa$.

source.place: Agent cardinality and indexing details for Lemma 5.4.6.3, first paragraph of proof.

proof.text: We construct compatible diagrams $q:N(E)\to\mathcal X$, $s:N(O)\to\mathcal Z$, and $Q:N(\kappa)\to\mathcal Y$, with restrictions $Q|_{N(E)}=fq$ and $Q|_{N(O)}=gs$ holding exactly as simplicial maps, using the fixed-boundary representatives of steps 1–2. For stage $0$, choose $x_0\in\mathcal X$ by filteredness for the empty shape and set $Q(0)=f(x_0)$. Stage $1$ is handled separately. Choose $z_0\in\mathcal Z$. Filteredness of $\mathcal Y$ gives a vertex $y$ and arrows $f(x_0)\to y$ and $g(z_0)\to y$, by applying the cocone definition to two discrete vertices. Apply $\kappa$-cofinality of $g$ to the one-point diagram $z_0$ and its cocone $g(z_0)\to y$. This supplies $z_0\to z_1$ and a morphism of cocones with vertex arrow $y\to g(z_1)$. Composing with $f(x_0)\to y$ gives the diagram $Q$ on $\{0<1\}$, and set $s(1)=z_1$. The coherent composition is an inner-horn filler. In particular we have not treated the empty preceding odd part as weakly contractible.

source.place: Agent expansion of the initial stages omitted from Lemma 5.4.6.3.

proof.text: For a successor stage $\alpha=\beta+1\geq2$, let $T$ be $E\cap\alpha$ if $\alpha$ is even, and $O\cap\alpha$ if $\alpha$ is odd; let $v$ denote the existing diagram into $\mathcal X$ or $\mathcal Z$ respectively, and $F$ the corresponding functor $f$ or $g$. The set $T$ is nonempty (it contains $0$ in the even case and $1$ in the odd case), and its nerve is weakly contractible: the arrows from its least element to every vertex define a natural transformation from the constant functor to its identity, contracting the nerve. Its nerve is $\kappa$-small by step 3. The restriction of $Q$ to $T\cup\{\beta\}$ gives a cocone on $Fv$ with vertex $Q(\beta)$. Apply $\kappa$-cofinality of $F$ to $v$ and this cocone. We obtain a cocone on $v$ with new vertex $v_\alpha$ and a morphism from the displayed target cocone to its image. By step 2 the latter is a diagram on the ordered set $T\cup\{\beta,\alpha\}$. It agrees with $Q$ on $T\cup\{\beta\}$ and with the image of the new source cone on $T\cup\{\alpha\}$. Put $B=T\cup\{\beta\}\subseteq\alpha$. This $B$ is cofinal since it contains the greatest element $\beta$ of $\alpha$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-linear-cofinal-cone-extension] to $A_0=\alpha$ with new vertex $\alpha$: the old $Q$ on $N(\alpha)$ and the just constructed cone on $N(B)$ extend to $N(\alpha+1)$. This extends the matching source diagram and all of $Q$, retaining every earlier simplex.

source.place: Agent expansion of the successor induction in Lemma 5.4.6.3, printed pp. 445-446.

proof.text: Let $0<\alpha<\kappa$ be a limit ordinal. This is an even stage. The existing even diagram $q|_{N(E\cap\alpha)}$ has $\kappa$-small domain, so filteredness of $\mathcal X$ supplies a cocone with new vertex $q(\alpha)$; by step 1 it is replaced by a sharp-join representative with the same diagram and vertex, a map on $N((E\cap\alpha)\cup\{\alpha\})$ extending $q|_{N(E\cap\alpha)}$. Its image under $f$ gives a cone extending $Q|_{N(E\cap\alpha)}$. The subset $E\cap\alpha$ is cofinal in $\alpha$, since for any $\gamma<\alpha$ the next even ordinal is still below the limit $\alpha$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-linear-cofinal-cone-extension] to $A_0=\alpha$ and $B=E\cap\alpha$. It extends the old $Q$ together with this chosen cone to $N(\alpha+1)$. Leave the odd diagram unchanged. This uses a cocone supplied by filteredness, rather than a colimit of the preceding diagram (which need not be $\kappa$-filtered).

source.place: Agent expansion of the limit induction in Lemma 5.4.6.3, printed p. 445.

proof.text: Perform the preceding recursion for all $\alpha<\kappa$. At a limit stage, the already defined portion is the union of its earlier portions, and at each successor the extension fixes that union. These unions define simplicial maps, because every simplex of an ordinal nerve uses finitely many vertices and is therefore contained in a bounded earlier portion; faces and degeneracies are inherited from the same portions. The source diagrams have the same compatibility. We obtain the three diagrams $q,s,Q$ of step 4 on their full nerves, without choosing any additional coherence at the end.

source.place: Agent explicit union step in the transfinite recursion of Lemma 5.4.6.3.

proof.text: Choose colimiting cocones on $q,s,Q$ with vertices $x,z,y$, respectively. These exist by the hypotheses because all three shapes are $\tau$-small and $\kappa$-filtered, as checked in step 3. Preservation makes the image cocones with vertices $f(x)$ and $g(z)$ colimiting for the two restrictions of $Q$. For the inclusion $N(E)\to N(\kappa)$ and any $\gamma<\kappa$, the comma quasicategory of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-comma-criterion] is the nerve of the tail $\{e\in E:\gamma\leq e\}$. Indeed its objects are exactly pairs $(e,\gamma\leq e)$ and its arrows are the order comparisons; there are no nonidentity equivalences in these posets to add identifications in the homotopy pullback. The tail is nonempty by unboundedness of $E$ and has a least element. The arrows from that element to every other element give a natural transformation from the constant functor to the identity and hence a contraction of its nerve. For $N(O)\to N(\kappa)$ the comma has objects $(o,\gamma\leq o)$ and order arrows, so it is the nerve of $\{o\in O:\gamma\leq o\}$. Unboundedness of $O$ makes this tail nonempty; its least element gives the constant-to-identity contraction. Thus the cited criterion applies to each inclusion and says that the cocone on $Q$ with vertex $y$, restricted to each parity, is colimiting. The indexing nerves are small by step 3; no ambient cocompleteness is needed.

source.place: Agent expansion of the colimit comparison in Lemma 5.4.6.3, printed p. 445.

proof.text: The restricted cocone on $fq$ with vertex $y$ and the image cocone with vertex $f(x)$ are both colimiting, hence initial in the coherent cocone quasicategory. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] the full subcategory of initial objects is a contractible Kan complex. It follows that these cocones are equivalent; evaluation at the vertices gives an equivalence $a:f(x)\simeq y$. The restricted cocone on $gs$ with vertex $y$ and the image cocone with vertex $g(z)$ are also initial in their coherent cocone quasicategory. The cited contractible-Kan-complex assertion makes these two cocones equivalent, and evaluating at the vertices gives $b:g(z)\simeq y$. The composite $b^{-1}\circ a$ is the required equivalence $f(x)\simeq g(z)$.
